document.note: [Secret] Intelligence community assumes bin Laden is alive because al-Qaeda could not keep his death secret. Wolfowitz disputes this, arguing al-Qaeda communicates effectively without detection, and warns of overreliance on a classified tracking capability ('the drunk looking for keys under the lamppost').

events.description: Wolfowitz sends Rumsfeld a memo, 'Al Qaeda Ops Sec', arguing al-Qaeda can communicate internally and that the US may be open to deliberate manipulation by the terrorists. The text gives the date as 2001, which appears to be an OCR or typing error; the document header and publication date point to 2002.

Wolfowitz sends memo 'Al Qaeda Ops Sec' to Rumsfeld questioning intelligence community assumptions that bin Laden is alive and warning that al-Qaeda may deliberately manipulate US intelligence collection. (Document date typed as 2001 but stamped 2002.)
Memo declassified by Records & Declass Division, WHS under EO 12958.

relationships.quote: the main explanation offered by the intelligence community is that his death would be too important a fact for them to be able to keep it secret.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is treated as al-Qaeda's central figure, whose death or survival would be communicated within the organization.
relationships.quote: they would have to communicate with one another about bin Laden's death, they would also have to communicate with one another about his survival.

relationships.detail: Al Qaeda is described as aware of US intelligence collection and potentially able to manipulate it.
relationships.quote: the terrorists know that we do this... we are susceptible to deliberate manipulation by the terrorists

sources_cited: US intelligence community assessments on bin Laden's survival
key_claims: The intelligence community assumes bin Laden is alive because his death could not be kept secret, yet his survival would be equally hard to conceal.
Wolfowitz argues that if al-Qaeda would have to communicate about bin Laden's death, it would also have to communicate about his survival.
Al-Qaeda is able to communicate within its organization.
The terrorists know that the US monitors their communications.
The US is susceptible to deliberate manipulation by the terrorists.
